On the Patriots' side, running back TreVeyon Henderson hasn't practiced since Aug. 24 due to an ankle issue, forcing reliance on Rhamondre Stevenson and depth like Corey Kiner amid questions about backfield depth per ESPN's Mike Reiss. Both squads listed multiple limited participants, highlighting short-week prep challenges ahead of the season start.

news.hook: With their season opener against the Patriots just days away, the Seahawks brought back a familiar face to shore up their safety position amid injury concerns.
news.name: Seahawks Re-Sign Safety D’Anthony Bell to Practice Squad for Depth
news.summary: The Seattle Seahawks signed veteran safety D’Anthony Bell, 29, back to their practice squad on Saturday, releasing undrafted rookie outside linebacker Marvin Jones Jr. to make room. Bell, who played 14 games with two starts for Seattle last season before stints with the Panthers, adds valuable depth alongside AJ Finley, Rodney Thomas II, and Maxen Hook. Rookie Nick Emmanwori's ankle injury clouds his Week 1 status, making Bell's system familiarity and special teams skills a smart insurance move as the team preps for Wednesday's rematch with New England.

news.name: 49ers Embrace Melbourne While Rams Plan Quick Trip for Historic NFL Clash
news.summary: The San Francisco 49ers arrived early in Melbourne for a full week of workouts, community events like a Bunnings sausage sizzle, and MCG visits, building fan goodwill ahead of the NFL's first regular-season game in Australia on September 11. The Los Angeles Rams, as the home team, will fly in close to kickoff at the 100,000-seat Melbourne Cricket Ground and leave soon after, a strategy coach Sean McVay says includes the full roster like Aaron Donald. With tickets sold out fast and crowds expected to heavily favor the 49ers in red, the Rams face a tough road-like atmosphere in this high-stakes season opener between last year's playoff teams.

news.hook: Josh McDaniels didn't hold back, pointing the finger squarely at himself for the Patriots' offensive woes in last February's Super Bowl defeat.
news.name: McDaniels Takes Blame for Patriots' Super Bowl Loss Ahead of Rematch
news.summary: The New England Patriots offensive coordinator accepted full responsibility for their 29-13 Super Bowl LX loss to the Seattle Seahawks, where quarterback Drake Maye faced six sacks and constant pressure. Speaking before Wednesday's Week 1 rematch at Lumen Field, McDaniels highlighted offseason fixes like adding Alijah Vera-Tucker and shifting lineup pieces to bolster pass protection after Maye was sacked 20 times in the playoffs. He expressed confidence in rookies like Will Campbell and a revamped unit facing Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald's top-ranked defense, calling it a fresh start for the new season.

news.name: Puka Nacua Expected to Play for Rams in Australia Opener Despite Soreness
news.summary: Los Angeles Rams coach Sean McVay said wide receiver Puka Nacua, who switched to jersey number 12 this season, is on track to play Thursday in the U.S. (Friday morning local time) at Melbourne Cricket Ground despite core muscle soreness and a pending NFL conduct review. Offensive tackle Alaric Jackson is also expected to be available, while both face league scrutiny over separate off-field incidents but avoided the commissioner's exempt list. The team is prepping carefully for the historic matchup, with defensive stars Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett set to practice soon, boosting quarterback Matthew Stafford's options.

news.name: Bill Plaschke Predicts Perfect Rams Season and Super Bowl Win
news.summary: Los Angeles Times columnist Bill Plaschke wrote that the Rams will finish 17-0 in the regular season and then sweep the playoffs at home, capping it with Super Bowl LXI on Valentine’s Day. He points to their favorable schedule, quarterback Matthew Stafford, coach Sean McVay, receiver Puka Nacua, and Aaron Donald's return from retirement as the keys to an undefeated run.
